fields.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
fields.note: The document supports the source-of-income bar, the protected classes, the Section 8 example, the advertising ban and the 180-day and two-year filing periods. It does not mention the $10,000 first-offense fine or the landlord's right to refuse for insufficient income, oversized family, zoning-violating occupancy or poor credit.

fields.quoted_span:
You may file a complaint with us for free within 180 days
of the date of the alleged violation.
fields.note: The 180-day Division complaint and the two-year Superior Court period are supported. The document does not mention fines up to $10,000 for a first offense.
The field is empty and the document gives no effective date.

fields.quoted_span:
The Division on Civil Rights enforces the New Jersey
Law Against Discrimination.
fields.note: The brochure describes the LAD in the present tense as currently enforced. It does not state a status explicitly.

fields.quoted_span:
The rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family
dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied
by the owner as his/her residence at the time of such
rentals;
fields.note: The general scope, the owner-occupied two-family exemption, the room-rental exemption, the religious-organization exemption and the familial-status exemption for older persons are all supported. The single-sex residence exemption does not appear in this document; it comes from D067.
The document never cites N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g). It names the Law Against Discrimination and cites only N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm, for the definition of older persons.
